The License tab now has a Manage Subscription button that opens the Polar customer portal in a new tab. Cancel auto-renewal, update your card, switch plans, or resubscribe — all without leaving WordPress admin. Snake-case + REST/React parity to MHM Rentiva v4.32.0.

documents.t: A two-day cross-plugin sprint that hardened the Rentiva (and Currency Switcher) Pro licensing layer against source-edit bypass attacks. Three Rentiva client releases (v4.30.0 / v4.30.1 / v4.30.2) shipped alongside four license-server releases (v1.9.0 → v1.9.3) and three Currency Switcher releases (v0.5.0 / v0.5.1 / v0.5.2). Live-deployed and verified end-to-end on mhmrentiva.com + wpalemi.com.
documents.s: License Security Hardening Sprint: Rentiva v4.30.0 → v4.30.2 (with mhm-license-server v1.9.0–v1.9.3 and CS v0.5.x)

Esta es una versión mayor y la primera compilación de Pro publicada desde la 5.2.3, a finales de julio. A la mayoría de los propietarios de sitios les bastan dos frases: actualiza primero MHM Rentiva a la 6.1.3 y después Pro, y tus datos se migrarán solos la próxima vez que abras la administración. Todos los demás —cualquiera que tenga código personalizado enganchado a Pro— tienen antes una breve lista que leer, porque han cambiado los nombres de 70 hooks y nada te avisa cuando uno deja de ejecutarse.
documents.s: Rentiva Pro 6.0.0 — Todo tiene nombres coherentes y la suspensión por fin significa suspensión

documents.t: Esta versión gira casi por completo en torno a una pregunta: qué ocurre cuando se elimina una cuenta. En la 6.0.0, la respuesta era peor de lo que debería en tres puntos distintos, y uno de ellos destruía los mensajes de un cliente en sitios que ni siquiera habían comprado la función de cumplimiento normativo. Actualiza primero MHM Rentiva a la 6.1.4 y después Pro. Esta vez no hay migración de datos ni cambios de nombre de hooks.
documents.s: Rentiva Pro 6.1.0 — Un botón de eliminación que solo un cliente puede pulsar

documents.t: Los vendedores tienen un panel propio, y el dinero que hay detrás pasa a una base común: una sola moneda en el libro contable y reembolsos que retiran exactamente la comisión que se abonó. Actualiza primero MHM Rentiva a la 6.1.5 y después Pro. Si Pro encuentra una versión anterior de Rentiva, se desactiva a sí mismo con un aviso y no crea nada.
documents.s: Rentiva Pro 6.2.0: un panel propio para los vendedores, una sola moneda en el libro contable y reembolsos que revierten la comisión exactamente

documents.t: 6.3.0 protege lo que entregan los vendedores: los IBAN, los documentos de identidad y los documentos de los vehículos se cifran y se mantienen fuera de la biblioteca de medios. Los mensajes se reconstruyen como conversaciones, y la gestión de vendedores incorpora una página de detalle del vendedor y un único lugar para todos los ajustes de vendedores. Actualiza primero MHM Rentiva (Lite) a la 6.2.0 y después Pro. Rentiva Pro 6.1.0 o anterior se detiene con un error en el panel del vendedor junto a Rentiva 6.2.0, así que haz las dos actualizaciones una tras otra.
documents.s: Rentiva Pro 6.3.0: IBAN y documentos de vendedores cifrados en reposo, mensajes reconstruidos como conversaciones y todos los ajustes de vendedores en un solo lugar

documents.t: 6.4.0 hace que las transferencias cobren lo que indican tus ajustes. El carrito de transferencias ahora calcula el precio de cada transferencia en el servidor y cobra el anticipo configurado en Ajustes > Transferencia; antes, tomaba el precio del navegador y siempre cobraba el importe completo. Los widgets de Pro muestran vistas previas seguras en los editores, y los correos electrónicos de Pro reciben nombres traducidos y el idioma del sitio. No se ejecuta ningún paso de base de datos al actualizar. Actualiza primero MHM Rentiva (Lite) a 6.3.0 y después Pro. Junto a Rentiva 6.2.1 o anterior, Pro 6.4.0 desactiva sus funciones hasta que se actualice Rentiva, así que haz las dos actualizaciones una tras otra.
documents.s: Rentiva Pro 6.4.0: las transferencias cobran el anticipo que configuras, el carrito de transferencias se calcula en el servidor y vistas previas seguras en los editores

documents.t: La 6.5.0 corrige cómo se gestionan el dinero de los vendedores, las cancelaciones y los datos personales. La comisión ahora va al vendedor propietario del vehículo reservado; antes, podía ir al cliente que hizo la reserva. Un reembolso solo revierte una comisión que realmente se haya abonado. Los mensajes, los datos de vendedores y los registros de consentimiento aparecen ahora en las herramientas de privacidad de WordPress, y los botones "Solicitar exportación de datos" y "Solicitar borrado de datos" de Mi cuenta inician una solicitud de privacidad que se confirma por correo electrónico. Activar "Exigir acuerdo de vendedor" ahora siempre muestra un acuerdo, con una plantilla inicial cuando el texto está vacío. Los informes y las analíticas de vendedores siguen la zona horaria del sitio. Pro 6.5.0 requiere WordPress 7.0 o posterior y Rentiva (Lite) 6.4.0 o posterior: actualiza primero Lite y después Pro.
documents.s: Rentiva Pro 6.5.0: comisión abonada al vendedor correcto, solicitudes de privacidad por correo electrónico, acuerdo de vendedor funcional e informes en la zona horaria del sitio

documents.t: v4.33.0 closes three holes left over from the v4.31.0 RSA token migration: 22 callsites that bypassed the token check, a misleading License Admin message, and the impossibility of testing Pro features locally without running a license server.

A focused patch bundling three fixes around vehicle admin and the Featured Vehicles surface — the Lifecycle meta box now identifies the vendor by name, the Featured Vehicles slider stops flickering on short lists, and Featured Vehicles gains a "View All" link in parity with Vehicles Grid.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.33.1 — Search Polish & Vendor Name Fix

documents.t: A pure translation patch. The Vendor surface in Turkish moves from Satıcı (literally "one who sells") to Bayi (dealer / authorized agency) across the entire catalog — Rentiva is a rental marketplace, not a sales platform, and "Satıcı" read awkwardly throughout the admin and vendor-facing screens.

The homepage now has a proper sales surface for VIP transfer routes. v4.34.0 ships a [rentivapopularroutes] shortcode + Gutenberg block + Elementor widget — three surfaces sharing one canonical renderer — that show A → B route cards (origin → destination, average duration, distance, starting price) with an admin "🌟 Vitrine Koy" pin checkbox to control which routes appear.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.34.0 — Popular Transfer Routes Showcase

documents.t: A small but high-leverage patch on top of v4.34.0. Popular Routes cards are now clickable, and clicking one deep-links into the transfer-search form with origin and destination pre-filled. The visitor's path goes from "see a route I want → find the search form → re-pick the same locations from a dropdown of seven → add date/time → submit" down to "click the route → add date/time → submit."
documents.s: Rentiva v4.34.1 — Popular Routes Clickable Cards

documents.t: A pure CSS hotfix on top of v4.34.1. The favorite (heart) and compare icons on the transfer-search results page rendered as oversized solid-blue blocks instead of the small round white icons used on the rental grid/list. v4.34.2 restores parity.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.34.2 — Transfer-card icon styling hotfix

documents.t: A shared infrastructure for vendor → admin reports lands in v4.35.0. Five contexts, one custom table, one shared modal, one admin "Bayi Raporları" page. Plus the withdrawal/pause reason capture flow: when a vendor withdraws a vehicle and explains why, the penalty is suspended until an admin reviews the appeal — accept, the vendor keeps their score; reject, the penalty applies retroactively.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.35.0 — Vendor Report & Appeal System

documents.t: Transfer customers can finally pick add-ons. v4.36.0 extends the existing vehicle_addon post type with a context taxonomy (rental / transfer / both) and three pricing types (per booking / per day / per passenger). When a customer clicks "Add to cart" on a transfer search result, a modal slides up showing the relevant add-ons with a live multiplier-aware total.

Every approved vendor now has a public face. v4.37.0 ships a dedicated profile page at /vendor// (or /bayi// on Turkish sites), wired up across a canonical shortcode, a Gutenberg block, and an Elementor widget — all delegating to a single renderer. Schema.org LocalBusiness JSON-LD goes out in `` so search engines and social previews can read the vendor as a discrete entity, not as a slice of the homepage.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.37.0 — Vendor Public Profile Page

documents.t: Three smoke-test findings on the freshly-shipped v4.37.0 vendor profile page are closed in v4.37.1: a badge that defaulted to "New Vendor" for every vendor regardless of their score, a misleading "X reviews" label whose number was actually the count of booking-time star ratings, and review stars that disappeared on the public profile when reviews were imported from third-party plugins.

Seven UX findings on the vendor profile page deferred from v4.37.0/v4.37.1 close in v4.37.2: a deterministic SVG initials avatar that replaces the Gravatar mystery-man silhouette without breaking third-party avatar plugins, a vehicle thumbnail cascade that falls back through featured image → gallery → compact card, an SEO defaults class that yields to Yoast / Rank Math / AIOSEO when present, a hero CTA stack with filterable URLs, scoped CSS class names, and a mobile breakpoint that finally collapses small screens to a single column.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.37.2 — Vendor profile UX polish

documents.t: A short patch to clear the CI red mark left behind by v4.37.2. A single WPCS sniff — "Opening PHP tag must be on a line by itself" — failed on the v4.37.2 hero template after merge. v4.37.3 refactors the block so the PHP opening tag stands alone. Lint-only — no behaviour change.

A public, Pro-gated vendor catalogue lands in Rentiva. Customers can now discover all your active vendors in one place — filter by city, badge status, and minimum rating; sort by reputation, recency, or alphabetically; click any card to land on the vendor's public profile (introduced in v4.37.0). This release closes the marketplace discovery loop.

A small but important patch on top of v4.38.0. After the Vendor Directory release we ran a /wp-conductor post-merge audit on the v4.37.0 → v4.38.0 chain — two real findings and a dormant production defect surfaced from the new test coverage. v4.38.1 closes them all so the six-release deploy bundle is clean.

A focused developer-experience fix. The Traefik migration from localhost:port to *.localhost domains silently broke automatic Pro dev mode on all local Docker stacks — v4.38.2 restores zero-config development.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.38.2 — Dev mode fix: Traefik *.localhost support

documents.t: The legacy jQuery / WPListTable Customers admin page is gone. v4.39.0 replaces it with a full React SPA backed by a dedicated REST API — live search, sortable columns, a slide-in detail panel, and bulk delete, all without page reloads.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.39.0 — Customers Page React SPA (Faz 2)

documents.t: The Pending Applications and IBAN Requests admin tabs have been completely rewritten as a React SPA backed by a dedicated REST API — eliminating full-page PHP renders and introducing 7 new REST endpoints for programmatic access.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.40.0 — Vendor Management Phase A: React SPA

documents.t: The Messages admin page has been completely rewritten as a React SPA, replacing the legacy jQuery/WPListTable implementation. Real-time filtering, bulk actions, thread view, reply forms, and settings management — all without page reloads.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.41.0 — Messages Phase 3: Full React SPA

documents.t: Adds the Payout Requests admin page, groups vendor-related menus at the sidebar bottom, and includes a round of PHP cleanup across the License and Setup Wizard admin pages.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.42.0 — Payout Requests page + admin cleanup

documents.t: Two additions to Vendor Management: a one-click Unsuspend action for suspended vendors, and a Rate History table in the Commission tab showing the full audit trail of platform-wide commission policies.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.43.0 — Vendor Unsuspend + Commission History

documents.t: A polish-and-fix release addressing three visual inconsistencies and one data bug found during QA of the v4.40.0–v4.43.0 React migration chain.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.44.0 — Admin UI polish + bug fixes

documents.t: A round of admin interface refinements: KPI stat card grid layout, developer mode banner placement, human-readable location type labels, and styled action links across Locations and Routes tables.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.45.0 — Admin UI polish: grids, labels, buttons

documents.t: A systematic frontend CSS hardening release. All 31 frontend shortcode CSS files now participate in the active theme's design token system and are protected against whitespace inheritance from the block editor's shortcode container.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.46.0 — Frontend CSS isolation strategy

documents.t: Urgent fix for a fatal error on the Vehicles and Bookings admin list pages introduced in v4.44.0. If you're on v4.44.0–v4.46.0, update immediately.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.47.0 — Critical fix: fatal error on Vehicles and Bookings pages

documents.t: Three mobile-responsive CSS fixes for the admin interface: Messages table card layout, KPI stat card grid collapse, and Reports date filter stack. All targeting real mobile viewports where the WP admin sidebar is collapsed.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.48.0 — Mobile responsive CSS fixes

documents.t: All admin React CSS breakpoints standardised at 782 px — the correct breakpoint that accounts for WordPress's admin sidebar width offset on mobile devices.
Support URLs updated to wpalemi.com, changelog backfilled for v4.40.0–v4.49.0, and README updated with the React SPA admin interface section.

Vendor Management completes its React SPA migration with Faz B: the Vendors, Commission, and Settings tabs are now fully client-side. Seven new REST endpoints, three new React components, and an N+1 query fix for vendor listing.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.51.0 — Vendor Management Faz B: Vendors, Commission & Settings React SPA

documents.t: The Export admin page is now a full React SPA. 780 lines of legacy PHP render code have been replaced with a REST-backed interface featuring live record preview, export history with per-entry delete, and a preserved admin-post.php CSV download flow.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.52.0 — Export Page React SPA

documents.t: Vendor Management mobile rendering fixes. The Vendors table was broken at 390px — columns crushed to ~40px causing vertical text — and now scrolls horizontally. Settings and Commission inputs respect container width at narrow widths.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.53.0 — Vendor Management Mobile CSS Polish

documents.t: Mobile rendering fixes for the Customers list, the Customer detail panel, and the Vendor Reports table, plus a currency-symbol HTML entity decode fix.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.54.0 — Customers + Vendor Reports Mobile Fixes

documents.t: KPI cards and table action buttons on the Shortcode Pages admin screen are now accessible at narrow widths.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.55.0 — Shortcode Pages Mobile Fixes

documents.t: Consistent gradient KPI cards now apply across all admin list pages. Vehicles, Bookings, Transfer, and Additional Services adopt the Dashboard/Reports blue/green/amber/grey gradient style.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.56.0 — Unified KPI Card Style Across Admin Pages

documents.t: Horizontal scroll wrappers added to the remaining admin tables that overflowed on narrow viewports.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.57.0 — Setup Wizard + Transfer Tables Mobile Scroll

documents.t: Critical fixes for remaining-payment double-tax and orphan WC orders after auto-cancel. Dashboard widgets gain status badges, plate, location, and a deposit/remaining split. The About > Support tab adds a GitHub Issues card, test stats, and a changelog accordion. The License page moves to a 2-column grid, and Messages adopt a React 18 chat bubble UI. 88 new Turkish translations.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.58.0 — Financial Bug Fixes, Dashboard Polish, Expanded i18n

documents.t: AutoComplete cron compared dropoffdate < NOW() at date-only granularity. MySQL cast YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD 0000, so any confirmed booking with a same-day dropoff was auto-completed at midnight — long before the actual return time. hasoverlap() then skipped these wrongly-completed bookings (status filter excluded 'completed'), allowing the same vehicle to be double-booked for the remaining rental hours. This release fixes the cron, adds defense-in-depth at hasoverlap(), opens a completed → inprogress Status transition, and ships a maintenance script to revert already-contaminated bookings.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.58.1 — Critical: Double-Booking Fix on Same-Day Returns

documents.t: TransferSearchEngine had no location filter — a search for an İstanbul route returned vehicles parked in Ankara and Antalya. This release adds city-based vehicle matching (route origin's city), reusing the rental module's 3-layer hybrid filter (vehicle → vendor inheritance → global default) via a new expandtocity mode. Plus a batch of UI/content polish: KPI spacing on list-table pages, dashboard card heights, About page hardening, and Vehicles calendar parity with the Bookings page.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.58.2 — Transfer City Filter + UI Polish

documents.t: Matured vendor payouts were silently skipped on single-site installs: a dead SaaS "control plane" gate in the matured-payout worker required a multi-tenant registry row that a normal install never provisions, so no scheduled payout ever finalized automatically. This release removes that gate — the worker now runs unconditionally — and clears out the unused multi-tenant orchestration scaffolding that caused it.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.60.0 — Matured Payout Fix + Dead SaaS Scaffolding Removal

documents.t: When you approve a vendor payout, Rentiva now generates a printable, sequentially-numbered payment statement for the period — earnings, the platform commission deducted from each, penalties, and the net paid — frozen as an immutable record and emailed to the vendor. This release also adds a vendor agreement acceptance gate on the application form, an "Added by" column that distinguishes operator and vendor vehicles, and one-click day blocking in the Monthly Reservation Calendar.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.61.0 — Vendor Payout Statements with Commission Breakdown

documents.t: When a Pro license expires, catalog items added during the Pro period that exceed the Lite plan limits — vehicles, add-on services, and transfer routes — are now automatically hidden from the public site instead of staying live. Data is never deleted; everything is restored the moment you upgrade to Pro again.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.62.0 — Lite Downgrade Catalog Overflow Enforcement

documents.t: A patch release fixing the Lite VIP transfer route limit counter, which silently failed to enforce the route cap on installs using the current routes table.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.62.1 — Lite VIP Transfer Route Limit Counter Fix

documents.t: An internal hardening patch ensuring the Lite vehicle-limit counter reflects the true vehicle count independently of the public overflow-hiding filter.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.62.2 — Lite Vehicle-Limit Counter Hardening

documents.t: A patch release fixing a checkout bug where switching the payment-type option from "Full Payment" back to "Deposit Payment" left the remaining balance stuck at zero.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.62.3 — Checkout Deposit Remaining-Amount Restore Fix

documents.t: Admins can now generate and email a payable link for a booking's remaining amount, and full-payment-only bookings no longer get mislabeled "Deposit" in a mixed cart.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.63.0 — Admin Remaining-Payment Link + Payment-Type Label Fix

documents.t: Fixes blank revenue charts, a corrupted Reports KPI value, and a bug where saving Messages settings from one tab silently reset the others.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.63.1 — Chart Rendering, KPI Corruption, and Settings-Tab Data-Loss Fixes

documents.t: Fixes vendor commission recording, adds an automatic 7-day clearing mechanism so earnings actually become withdrawable, corrects refund balance math, and fixes a vendor dashboard KPI card that always showed zero.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.63.2 — Vendor Commission Clearing & Refund Balance Fixes

documents.t: Admins can now override the commission rate per vendor or per vehicle, and configure the volume-discount tier thresholds directly from the admin panel — closing the last three previously UI-less layers of the commission rate hierarchy. Also includes three commission-accuracy fixes and a schema migration guard found during release verification.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.64.0 — Commission Rate Overrides (Vendor & Vehicle) and Tier Configuration

documents.t: Fixes the admin panel's quick Dark Mode switch silently blanking Support Phone/Hours/Email and resetting Brand Name, and cleans up a residual settings-pollution artifact left behind by an older migration.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.64.1 — Dark Mode Toggle Field Clobber Fix

documents.t: Fixes near-invisible text in Dark Mode and 6 example placeholders that could never be translated, no matter the site's language.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.64.2 — Dark Mode Contrast + Un-translatable Placeholder Fixes

documents.t: A full contrast audit across every Settings tab, fixing roughly 15 more dark-mode readability issues beyond the previous patch.
documents.s: Rentiva v4.64.3 — Full Dark Mode Contrast Audit

documents.t: MHM Rentiva's first public release, free to download: the complete rental core with no artificial limits, no third-party requests, and full WordPress.org coding-standards compliance.

A coupled patch release that fixes the data-export screen. Lite ships the shared bundle (v5.0.1); Pro ships the logic (v5.0.2). The free plugin's own behaviour is unchanged — the export screen is a Pro feature.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.0.1 / Pro v5.0.2 — Export screen fixes

documents.t: A hardening pass ahead of the WordPress.org listing. The free plugin's features and behaviour are unchanged — what changed is how carefully it handles input, output and permissions, and what it no longer ships.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.1.0 / Pro v5.1.0 — Security hardening, and no third-party calls at all

documents.t: A small follow-up to v5.1.0, continuing the pass ahead of the WordPress.org listing. Nothing about how the plugin behaves changes here — this is the kind of release that is worth publishing precisely because it is uneventful.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.1.1 / Pro v5.1.1 — Compliance hygiene, no behaviour change

documents.t: The largest release in the 5.x line so far. Permission checks now test the specific record a request names instead of a general capability, the admin markup is filtered as it is printed, the Dashboard and Vehicle Settings screens are redesigned — and a long list of controls that claimed to do something, but were connected to nothing, has been removed.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.2.0 / Pro v5.2.0 — Seventeen security switches that did nothing, and the ones that now do

documents.t: A patch release about honesty. The dashboard chart was named after something it does not measure, and a set of admin strings was being shipped in English despite having been translated months ago. Both are fixed — and the second one turned out to have a cause worth writing down.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.2.1 / Pro v5.2.1 — A chart that says what it counts, and translations that ship

documents.t: A patch release with one uncomfortable admission in it. Preparing for the WordPress.org submission, we ran our WooCommerce control checklist against the whole codebase for the first time — and found that we had never answered WooCommerce's compatibility questions at all.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.2.2 / Pro v5.2.2 — What we tell WooCommerce, and one thing we were telling it wrong

documents.t: Another patch on the way to the WordPress.org submission, and another release where the interesting part is not the bug we fixed but what we found while checking whether we had described it honestly.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.2.3 / Pro v5.2.3 — A table WordPress was never really looking at, and a privacy notice that named the wrong things

documents.t: A small release with a simple theme: fitting into WordPress rather than competing with it.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.2.4 — The menu moves down, and every link out of your site is now written down

documents.t: MHM Rentiva ya está publicado en el directorio de plugins de WordPress.org. Lo instalas como instalarías cualquier otra cosa (lo buscas, haces clic en instalar) y, a partir de ahí, WordPress lo mantiene actualizado.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.0.7: MHM Rentiva ya está en el directorio de plugins de WordPress.org

documents.t: Si un cliente pagaba y luego cancelaba, Rentiva marcaba la reserva como pendiente de reembolso y se quedaba ahí. No se movía dinero. Alguien tenía que darse cuenta y reembolsarlo a mano. A partir de la 6.1.0, la cancelación lleva el reembolso hasta tu pasarela de pago.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.1.0: cancelar una reserva pagada ahora devuelve el dinero

documents.t: Si los campos de detalles de tus vehículos se configuraron antes de la 6.1.2, añadir imágenes a la galería y pulsar Actualizar podía borrar la galería que acababas de añadir. La 6.1.3 lo soluciona y no te pide nada: ni cambios en la base de datos ni volver a guardar los ajustes. Basta con instalarla.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.1.3: las galerías de vehículos dejan de desaparecer

documents.t: Si un invitado reservaba contigo primero y creaba una cuenta después, la pantalla Clientes no podía ver esa reserva. La fila del cliente mostraba 0 reservas, su dinero nunca llegaba a las tarjetas de resumen de la parte superior y "Ver reservas" mostraba una lista vacía. La 6.1.4 lo corrige y no te pide nada: ningún cambio en la base de datos ni volver a guardar los ajustes.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.1.4: una reserva vinculada por ID ya no desaparece de la pantalla Clientes

documents.t: Si usas MHM Currency Switcher junto con Rentiva, un solo clic en la limpieza de la base de datos de Rentiva podía borrar los precios fijos de tus productos. La 6.1.5 corrige esto, hace que la limpieza se niegue a eliminar nada que no haya podido copiar antes en una copia de seguridad y soluciona un filtro de Reservas que nunca terminaba de cargar. Está publicada en WordPress.org, así que WordPress te la ofrece como una actualización normal; no hace falta volver a guardar nada después.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.1.5 — La limpieza de la base de datos ya no elimina lo que no le pertenece

documents.t: 6.2.0 reúne cuatro semanas de trabajo. Los mensajes de contacto pasan a una pantalla propia y sus archivos adjuntos a una carpeta privada, se retira el panel del cliente independiente en favor de Mi cuenta, y los ajustes de bloques y Elementor que se guardaban pero nunca llegaban a la página ahora surten efecto. Está publicada en WordPress.org, así que WordPress te la ofrece como una actualización normal. ¿Usas Rentiva Pro? Pro 6.1.0 o anterior se detiene con un error en el panel del vendedor junto a esta versión: actualiza Pro a 6.3.0 justo después.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.2.0: los mensajes de contacto tienen su propia pantalla, se retira el panel del cliente y ahora se aplican los ajustes de bloques y Elementor que se ignoraban

documents.t: 6.2.1 es una corrección de privacidad para los sitios que crean páginas con Elementor. Los widgets de Elementor de Rentiva podían dejar los datos de la cuenta de la persona que guardaba una página dentro del texto almacenado de esa página, donde la búsqueda del sitio podía encontrarlos. Esta versión lo evita y limpia las páginas ya afectadas. Está publicada en WordPress.org, así que WordPress te la ofrece como una actualización normal. Si usas Elementor, actualiza ahora y sigue los dos pasos de «Después de actualizar».
documents.s: Rentiva 6.2.1 — Los widgets de Elementor ya no escriben los datos de la cuenta del usuario que guarda en el texto almacenado de una página

documents.t: 6.3.0 reúne el trabajo realizado desde la 6.2.1. Los alquileres incorporan un ajuste de anticipo para todo el sitio, un vehículo configurado solo para transferencia ya no se puede alquilar y los widgets de Rentiva muestran vistas previas seguras en los editores de Elementor y de bloques. Los ajustes de correo electrónico que se guardaban pero se ignoraban ahora se aplican, y el formulario de reserva comprueba en el servidor lo que antes tomaba del navegador. Al actualizar no se ejecuta ningún paso en la base de datos. La 6.3.1 llegó el mismo día con una corrección para sitios con Elementor: consulta el final de esta entrada. Está publicada en WordPress.org, así que WordPress te la ofrece como una actualización normal. ¿Usas Rentiva Pro? Actualiza Pro a la 6.4.0 justo después.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.3.0: anticipo de alquiler para todo el sitio, vistas previas seguras en el editor, ajustes de correo electrónico que se aplican y un formulario de reserva que comprueba el servidor

documents.t: 6.4.0 rediseña las páginas que un visitante ve primero y hace que el precio que aparece en pantalla sea el precio que se cobra. La barra de búsqueda, la página de resultados y la tarjeta de vehículo siguen el nuevo diseño del front-end, con un filtro de categoría, etiquetas de filtro, una barra de comparación y un panel de filtros en los móviles. Con fechas de búsqueda, cada tarjeta muestra el total del alquiler. El formulario de reserva presupuesta exactamente lo que cobra WooCommerce: los precios por temporada ahora llegan al pago y los impuestos solo proceden de WooCommerce. Mi cuenta también sigue el nuevo diseño. Rentiva ahora necesita WordPress 7.0 o posterior, y debes vaciar la caché de páginas después de actualizar; consulta los recuadros de abajo. Está publicado en WordPress.org, así que WordPress te lo ofrece como una actualización normal; la página de WordPress.org tiene ahora ocho capturas de pantalla. ¿Usas Rentiva Pro? Actualiza Pro a la 6.5.0 después de esta versión; Pro 6.4.x sigue funcionando hasta entonces.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.4.0: nueva búsqueda, página de resultados y tarjeta de vehículo, un presupuesto de reserva igual al cargo y WordPress 7.0

documents.t: 6.4.1 es una pequeña actualización que corrige lo que un administrador lee en tres pantallas y lo que recibe un cliente nuevo. El resumen del calendario de reservas ahora muestra las horas de recogida y devolución, el total con la moneda de tu tienda y las fechas en el formato de tu sitio. Próximas operaciones del escritorio escribe sus fechas en el idioma de tu administración. Un cliente cuya cuenta crea WooCommerce recibe un solo correo de bienvenida en lugar de dos. No hay nada que configurar ni ningún paso en la base de datos. ¿Usas Rentiva Pro? No tienes que hacer nada: Pro 6.5.1 funciona con 6.4.1.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.4.1: un solo correo de bienvenida para una cuenta nueva, y el resumen del calendario de reservas y las fechas del escritorio mostrados correctamente

documents.t: MHM Rentiva v4.5.5 sürümü yayınlandı! Bu sürüm, kararlılık iyileştirmeleri, kritik performans düzeltmeleri ve dokümantasyon altyapısında büyük yenilikler içeriyor.
MHM Rentiva v4.6.0 sürümü yayınlandı! Bu sürüm, uzun zamandır beklenen VIP Transfer Modülü, gelişmiş rota yönetimi ve esnek fiyatlandırma motoru gibi büyük özellikler içeriyor.
MHM Rentiva v4.6.1 sürümü yayınlandı! Bu sürüm, veri bütünlüğü, güvenlik ve WooCommerce entegrasyonu konularında kritik iyileştirmeler içeren bir güvenlik ve kararlılık güncellemesidir.
MHM Rentiva v4.10.0 sürümü yayınlandı! Bu büyük güncelleme ile Gutenberg blokları ve kısa kodlar (shortcode) arasındaki tam eşlik (parity) sağlandı; 19/19 deterministic yüzey doğrulandı.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.10.0: Block/Shortcode Parity Stabilizasyonu

documents.t: MHM Rentiva v4.21.2 sürümü yayınlandı! Bu sürüm, eklentinin ticaret ve operasyon yeteneklerini kökten değiştiren "Vendor Management", "Financial Architecture" ve "VIP Transfer" modüllerini beraberinde getiriyor.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.21.2: Vendor Yönetimi ve Finansal Mimari Devrimi

documents.t: MHM Rentiva v4.23.0 sürümü yayınlandı! Bu sürüm, vendor'ların transfer hizmetlerini şehir bazlı yönetebilmesini sağlayan yeni bir mimari, kapsamlı Dashboard widget denetimi ve onlarca hata düzeltmesi getiriyor.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.23.0: Vendor Transfer Mimarisi & Dashboard Denetimi

documents.t: MHM Rentiva v4.23.1 surumu yayinlandi! Bu surum, vendor ayarlar sayfasinin tamamen yeniden tasarlanmasini, basvuru formundaki alan degisikliklerini, sehir secici bilesenlerin SelectWoo'ya donusturulmesini ve arac sigorta belgesi yukleme ozelligini icerir.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.23.1: Vendor Form Yeniden Tasarimi & Sehir SelectWoo Migrasyonu

documents.t: MHM Rentiva v4.24.0 sürümü yayınlandı! Bu sürüm, araçların tüm ömrü boyunca yönetilebileceği tam durum makinesi, vendor'ların araçlarını kendi kendine yönetebileceği AJAX self-servis uç noktaları ve adil rekabeti koruyan anti-gaming mekanizmaları getiriyor.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.24.0: Araç Yaşam Döngüsü Yönetimi & Vendor Self-Servis

documents.t: v4.25.0, vendor bildirimleri için yönetici panelinden düzenlenebilir e-posta şablonları getiriyor. 22 vendor bildirim şablonu artık Ayarlar ekranından özelleştirilebilir. Ayrıca Site Instance Check-in cron'u Cron İş Monitörü'ne eklendi ve weekly WP cron interval'inin güvenilir kaydı garanti altına alındı.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.25.0: Yönetici Tarafından Düzenlenebilir Vendor E-posta Şablonları

documents.t: v4.26.0, depozito ile oluşturulan rezervasyonlarda müşterilerin kalan bakiyeyi doğrudan Hesabım ekranından ödeyebilmesini sağlıyor. WooCommerce'in native ödeme altyapısı kullanıldığından aktif tüm ödeme yöntemleri otomatik olarak çalışıyor.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.26.0: Depozito Rezervasyonlarında Kalan Ödeme

documents.t: v4.26.1, v4.26.0 ile devreye giren rezervasyon-ödeme akışının üstüne gelen görsel tutarsızlıkları temizliyor. Araç detay sayfasından sepete, sepetten ödeme sayfasına kadar müşterinin gördüğü her ekranda kart, ikon ve hizalama sorunları giderildi. Fonksiyonel bir değişiklik yok — sadece deneyim daha temiz.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.26.1: Araç Detayları, Rezervasyon, Ödeme ve Sepet Görsel Cilası

documents.t: v4.26.2, eklenti kaldırıldığında arkada kalan tüm tabloların silinmesini sağlıyor, wp-cli bootstrap sırasındaki fatal hatayı gideriyor ve şema migration'ların artık sürüm değişikliğinde otomatik çalışmasını garantiliyor. Üç düzeltme de üretim ortamlarındaki sessiz sorunları hedefliyor.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.26.2: Tam Kaldırma Temizliği ve CLI Bootstrap Güçlendirmesi

documents.t: v4.26.3, listeleme/arama sayfalarındaki araç görsellerinin bulanık yüklenmesine neden olan responsive sizes hatasını, ayarlar sayfasındaki "kaydedildi" toast bildirimlerinin kesilip ekrandan taşmasını ve release ZIP'inden Chart.js'in çıkarılmasına yol açan .distignore kök-sabitleme hatasını gideriyor. Üçü de üretimde gözle görülen ama console.log'a düşmeyen sessiz sorunlardı.

documents.t: v4.27.0 is a milestone release completing the code quality audit ahead of submitting the plugin to the official WordPress.org plugin directory. The entire distributed codebase now passes the project's strict PHPCS ruleset with zero errors, zero warnings, and achieves zero errors against Plugin Check (PCP) — the official WordPress.org review tool. Four real defects uncovered during the process have also been closed.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.27.0: WordPress.org Submission Readiness — Zero PHPCS Errors, Zero PCP Errors

documents.t: A few hours after the v4.27.0 WordPress.org submission readiness release, a critical bug was caught: On an English WordPress site, the Vehicle Settings page was displaying Turkish labels. This is a global plugin; English is the primary language. The bug was submission-blocker severity. v4.27.1 fixes it.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.27.1: i18n Locale-Leak Hotfix — Vehicle Settings Labels No Longer Frozen at First-Install Language

The License tab now has a Manage Subscription button that opens the Polar customer portal in a new tab. Cancel auto-renewal, update your card, switch plans, or resubscribe — all without leaving WordPress admin. Snake-case + REST/React parity to MHM Rentiva v4.32.0.
documents.s: Currency Switcher v0.7.0 — Manage your subscription from the plugin

documents.t: Inside the License tab's License Management zone (visible when a Pro license is active), a third button joins the existing two: Manage Subscription — opens Polar customer portal (this release) Re-validate Now Deactivate License The plugin reaches Polar through the same license server already in use. No new external services contacted from your site's perspective. Schema and signature integrity remain RSA-protected (v0.6.0+ pipeline).

The button changes color based on how close your subscription is to renewal: Days remaining Color Intent > 30 Standard primary blue "Plenty of runway" ≤ 30 Yellow "Heads up — renewal is coming" ≤ 7 Amber + glow "Decide now" Expired (0) Amber + glow "Resubscribe to keep Pro" While the portal session is being minted (a brief async call), the button text becomes "Opening…" and the styling dims to communicate the click registered.

If the portal session can't be minted (server error, network blip, license revoked between page load and click), the button surfaces an in-tab notice instead of breaking: Subscription management is not available right now. Please try again later or contact support@wpalemi.com. No raw technical strings ever leak to end users.

New public method LicenseManager::create_customer_portal_session(string $return_url): array (snake_case parity to Rentiva's camelCase) New REST endpoint POST /mhm-currency/v1/license/manage-subscription (manage_options gated) New React state + callback in License.jsx, button rendered before Deactivate when isActive && license.maskedKey New CSS rules using compound selectors (.button.mhm-cs-license-warning / .mhm-cs-license-urgent) to avoid colliding with the existing .mhm-cs-license-warning alert pill 4 new translatable strings, all translated to Turkish

Component Required version mhm-license-server v1.11.0+ (new /customer-portal-session endpoint) mhm-polar-bridge v1.9.0+ (renewal reminder cron) WordPress 6.0+ PHP 7.4+ Older license-server versions without the customer-portal endpoint return a graceful in-tab notice instead of breaking.

Past-due / dunning notifications — Polar handles these directly via email. Yearly subscription renewal reminders — Polar sends these 7 days before renewal automatically. Monthly subscribers receive an additional 7-day-out reminder email from mhm-polar-bridge v1.9.0+, since Polar doesn't generate these for short billing cycles.

A two-day cross-plugin sprint that hardened the Rentiva (and Currency Switcher) Pro licensing layer against source-edit bypass attacks. Three Rentiva client releases (v4.30.0 / v4.30.1 / v4.30.2) shipped alongside four license-server releases (v1.9.0 → v1.9.3) and three Currency Switcher releases (v0.5.0 / v0.5.1 / v0.5.2). Live-deployed and verified end-to-end on mhmrentiva.com + wpalemi.com. Written before 6.0.0 This post is the record of a release that shipped before 6.0.0, which renamed the plugin's post types, taxonomies, options, meta keys and hooks. The identifiers below are the names those versions actually used, and they are kept that way on purpose. For the current names — and a conversion table — see the 6.0.7 release post.
documents.s: License Security Hardening Sprint: Rentiva v4.30.0 → v4.30.2 (with mhm-license-server v1.9.0–v1.9.3 and CS v0.5.x)

documents.t: The Rentiva plugin source ships on a public GitHub repository. A motivated attacker can clone, patch Mode::canUseVendorMarketplace() to return true;, and unlock Pro features without ever calling the license server. v1.8.0 closed cross-product key reuse (Currency Switcher key on Rentiva) but did nothing about source-edit bypass. v4.30.x raises the cost: a crack now has to forge an HMAC signature, host a fake validator, AND keep emitting fresh feature tokens — and even then, tokens expire within 24 hours. Five attack scenarios were used as the design target: Attack Mechanism Defended by Source-edit isActive() { return true; } Patch local Pro gate Layer 4 (feature token) Cross-product key reuse Use CS key on Rentiva Layer 1 (slug binding, v1.8.0) Empty product_slug body Strip the line, ride legacy compat Layer 1 hardened in v1.9.3 Fake activate POST from script No control over claimed site Layer 3 (reverse site validation) Pirated key + fake server DNS hijack to lookalike Layer 2 (response signing)
Companion to mhm-license-server v1.9.0 (Phase A — server-side three-layer defense).

ClientSecrets — resolves three new wp-config constants (MHM_RENTIVA_LICENSE_RESPONSE_HMAC_SECRET, MHM_RENTIVA_LICENSE_FEATURE_TOKEN_KEY, MHM_RENTIVA_LICENSE_PING_SECRET). ResponseVerifier — HMAC-SHA256 verification of every signed activate/validate response. Mirrors the server's recursive ksort + JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES|UNICODE canonicalization byte-for-byte — drift = legitimate responses look tampered. FeatureTokenVerifier — verifies {base64(json)}.{hmac} tokens issued by the server. 24h TTL. hasFeature($payload, $flag) accessor used by Mode gates. VerifyEndpoint — public REST route /wp-json/mhm-rentiva-verify/v1/ping answering the server's X-MHM-Challenge during reverse validation.

canUseVendorMarketplace(), canUseMessages(), canUseAdvancedReports(), canUseVendorPayout() now route through a single featureGranted() private helper that: Hard-checks isPro() first If FEATURE_TOKEN_KEY is unset → legacy isPro() fallback (existing customers don't break) Otherwise verifies the locally-stored feature token's HMAC Reads the specific flag from the payload (vendor_marketplace, messaging, advanced_reports, etc.) A return true; patch on isActive() no longer unlocks anything because the gate independently asks for a server-granted flag.

activate() request body now includes client_version = MHM_RENTIVA_VERSION. Server uses this for per-version reverse-validation enforcement (≥4.30.0 floor for Rentiva). Successful response's feature_token field is persisted alongside the existing license record. Daily verification cron refreshes the token on every tick.
6 new test files, 36 new tests across tests/Unit/Licensing/ and tests/Integration/Licensing/. Total: 776 / 2715, PHPCS clean, 3 new TR translations.

v4.30.0 made MHM_RENTIVA_LICENSE_PING_SECRET mandatory — without it, VerifyEndpoint returned 503 ping_secret_not_configured, and the license server then rejected activation with site_unreachable. Every customer site needed an operator-pinned secret in wp-config.php — unworkable for an end-customer product.
documents.s: v4.30.1 — Reverse Validation UX Fix (2026-04-25 morning)

documents.t: VerifyEndpoint::handle_ping() falls back to the per-activation site_hash (computed the same way LicenseManager::siteHash() does — sha256(home_url + site_url) JSON-encoded) when ClientSecrets::getPingSecret() returns empty. Server-side mhm-license-server v1.9.1+ applies the matching fallback in Security\SiteVerifier, so the HMAC challenge stays verifiable even though site_hash is technically not secret.

site_hash is publicly derivable, but tampering still fails because the reverse ping targets the claimed site_url. An attacker that doesn't control that domain cannot intercept the GET and reply with a forged HMAC, regardless of whether the HMAC key is private.
When MHM_RENTIVA_LICENSE_PING_SECRET IS defined, VerifyEndpoint still uses it — v4.30.0 deploys with operator config baked in keep working unchanged.
Two layered bugs in LicenseAdmin::admin_notices():
documents.s: v4.30.2 — License Notice Defensive Fix (2026-04-25 afternoon)

documents.t: Stale URL state (?license=error without &message=..., e.g. browser back/forward, bookmark, truncated copy-paste) leaked through the match's default arm into a sprintf("...: %s", '') call. Visible at the top of the License page even though the customer hadn't pressed anything.
documents.s: Bug A — Empty error_message rendered "License activation failed: " (with empty trailing space)

documents.t: site_unreachable, site_verification_failed, tampered_response, product_mismatch, product_slug_required had no friendly translations. They fell through to the same default arm, leaking raw technical codes to end users ("License activation failed: site_unreachable").
documents.s: Bug B — Missing match arms for v1.8.0+/v1.9.x server error codes

documents.t: Defensive guard: if ('' === $error_message) { break; } skips the notice entirely when there's no actionable code. Five new match arms with customer-friendly EN strings + Turkish translations. Generic default + data-error-code attribute: unknown future codes render "License activation failed. Please try again." with the technical code exposed via a data-error-code HTML attribute (debug / support only — never inline text).
While bumping the version, an audit caught that readme.txt Stable tag had been stuck at 4.30.0 — the v4.30.1 release accidentally skipped the bump. v4.30.2 corrects to 4.30.2.

tests/Unit/Licensing/LicenseAdminAdminNoticesTest.php — 5 new tests covering empty defense, site_unreachable mapping, generic default + data attribute, and two regression cases (activated, no-license-query). Total: 781 / 2726, PHPCS clean.

Chrome DevTools MCP scripted a tour of mhmrentiva.com after v4.30.2 deployment: URL Expected Live result ?license=error No notice (defensive guard) ✅ 0 notice elements ?license=error&message=site_unreachable Friendly EN message + data-error-code="site_unreachable", no raw code in inline text ✅ confirmed via DOM script ?license=error&message=imaginary_code_42 Generic message + data-error-code="imaginary_code_42", no raw code in inline text ✅ confirmed

v1.9.0 — Phase A: HMAC response signing, reverse site validation, feature token issuer (24h TTL). v1.9.1 — site_hash fallback inside Security\SiteVerifier::verify() (paired with v4.30.1 client). v1.9.2 — SecretManager::getPingSecret() opt-in only (no file fallback) — closed an asymmetric HMAC bug where the server auto-generated wp-uploads/mhm-license-secrets/ping.key while customers ran zero-config and the two paths produced different HMAC keys. v1.9.3 (CRITICAL) — LicenseActivator::activate() now hard-rejects empty product_slug against a slug-bound license row. The previous code path let a single source edit drop the slug from the request body and slide through both v1.8.0 binding AND v1.9.0 reverse validation (because REVERSE_VALIDATION_FLOOR[''] === null took the legacy-pass branch). Combined: 143 PHPUnit, 398 assertions, PHPCS clean on the server side. Three live attack scenarios were curl-verified against wpalemi.com after v1.9.3 deployment: Scenario Expected Live result product_slug removed from body product_slug_required reject ✅ confirmed Cross-product slug swap (CS slug + Rentiva site) site_unreachable (CS verify endpoint absent on Rentiva site) ✅ confirmed Correct flow regression 200 active ✅ confirmed

mhm-currency-switcher v0.5.0 (Phase C client) → v0.5.1 (CI hotfix: str_ends_with PHP 7.4 compat + OrderFilterTest WC_Order stub) → v0.5.2 (VerifyEndpoint site_hash fallback). Same five-attack-surface defense applied to CS Mode gates with eight feature flags (fixed_pricing, nav_menu_switcher, flag_library, geolocation, payment_restrictions, auto_rate_update, multilingual, rest_api_filter).

After this sprint, customers on Rentiva v4.30.1+ (and CS v0.5.2+): Just enter the license key and click Activate. No wp-config.php edits. Server-side three-layer defense (slug binding + response signing + reverse validation) is fully active. License notice messages are friendly and locale-aware; no raw technical jargon visible. Existing v4.27.x installs keep working unchanged through legacy fallback paths until they upgrade.

A sufficiently determined attacker running a cracked plugin binary on their own site with their own product-matching license can still patch Mode::canUse*() directly when the customer has not defined MHM_RENTIVA_LICENSE_FEATURE_TOKEN_KEY in wp-config.php (zero-config deployment intentionally accepts this trade-off). Closing the source-edit + zero-config gap requires asymmetric crypto (RSA-signed feature tokens, public key embedded in the plugin source — open-source-safe). This is deferred to mhm-license-server v1.10.0 + mhm-rentiva v4.31.0 + mhm-currency-switcher v0.6.0, planned post-launch.

patterns/license-defense-in-depth-stack.md — five-layer defense documentation, attack matrix, asymmetric crypto roadmap. patterns/admin-notice-url-state-defense.md — three-layer defense for redirect-after-action notices (empty guard + generic default + data attribute). patterns/release-zip-audit.md — three audits before tag/release; caught three ZIP leaks during this sprint (drafts/, bin/, *.po~). standards/i18n-workflow.md — updated with .po~ msgmerge backup pattern + .l10n.php deploy mandate. wp-conductor skill — new "Long Session / Chained Release Discipline" gate with per-release verification requirements (8 release chain on 2026-04-25 was the baseline failure that motivated this).
